SCRIPT-RUNTIMES-OUT-OF-PROCESS unit O1 (product; tests: #1167). Parent: `stack` s/161-lichen-env-tests2 65015486340270e6259535eeb9055786f472dda5 (CHILD-ENV-CLEAR closed). Tip a8397539d6e9e501c4b28a85fd76cf6771b77c77. - **Design:** lichen-orchestrator `machine-docs/plans/SCRIPT-RUNTIMES-O1-DESIGN-2026-10-08.md`, revision 2. It follows the operator's containment decision (`4bf1987a`) and positive-test decision (`157c5101`). - **Checked:** OK to build, with R2-D1 and R2-D2 (`machine-docs/reviews/SCRIPT-RUNTIMES-O1-DESIGN-CHECK-REV2-2026-10-08.md`). Both are in this PR. **Lua runs in a child process, lichen's own `script-runner` mode. Every script child (Python and Lua now) is contained by unprivileged mechanisms only, the same on every host and in a plain Docker container. There are no namespaces of any kind.** **Containment** (`lichen_flat_file::script_child`): - **Landlock files:** inherited from the site's confined worker, as before. - **Landlock network and scopes,** a second ruleset applied in `pre_exec`, with every right it asks for required: - with ABI 6, no abstract Unix sockets and no signals outside the child's domain; - from ABI 4, TCP per `script_network`, below. - **The empty environment** (CHILD-ENV-CLEAR). - **rlimits:** `RLIMIT_AS`, and an `RLIMIT_CPU` backstop of 10 CPU-minutes per child. - **`PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER`** on the child. The Lua runner reaps what comes back to it after each call. - **A seccomp filter,** built with seccompiler 0.5 (which needs only `libc`) and installed last in `pre_exec` under `no_new_privs`. It is inherited by everything the script starts. - **`EPERM`:** - `setsid` and `setpgid`, which closes SC-ESC1; - `unshare`, `setns`, and `clone` with any `CLONE_NEW*` flag; - `ptrace` and `process_vm_*`; - `mount`, `umount2` and `pivot_root`; - `bpf`, `perf_event_open` and `userfaultfd`; - `kexec_*` and the module calls; - the keyring calls. - **Sockets, as an allowlist (R2-D2):** under `public`, only an `AF_INET`/`AF_INET6` stream socket; under `off`, none. `socketpair` stays. - **`ENOSYS`:** `clone3` (libc falls back to `clone`, whose flags the filter reads) and io_uring. - **The process group killed in a loop:** SIGKILL to the group until it answers `ESRCH`, reaping the leader as it dies. The group's id cannot be reused while any member holds it, so the loop never reaches another group. Only SIGKILL stops a child (O1-D1). **The network:** - **`public`:** the parent serves lichen's proxy (S4's guard) on the host's loopback, on a port of its own. Landlock lets the child connect to that port only, and bind nothing. Where Landlock has no TCP rules (ABI < 4), the network is off, and the report's warning says so. - **`off`:** no socket at all, through the filter, whatever Landlock offers. - **`all`:** the host's network. - **The network namespace is gone,** with its in-namespace listener. **Older kernels (R2-D1; the operator's decision, revised):** - Landlock's signal scope (ABI 6, Linux 6.12) is the only thing that stops a script signalling the server. - Below it, scripts run as on a newer kernel, and lichen warns: once at startup in the log, and in each build's report as one warning line. `build/check` stays ok. - The Landlock layers follow the kernel's ABI: scopes from 6, TCP rules from 4. Below 4 the proxy's network is off, and the line says so. - `SECURITY-DEBT` `SC-SIG1` is accepted with a warning. - lichen-ci is ABI 7. - The requirement is documented in the lichen-mod skill and in lichen-flat-file's README. **The runner** (O-C3): - **Which executable:** `/proc/self/exe script-runner lua`. The worker's Landlock policy gains read and execute on that inode. - **Entry:** `lichen_cms::script_runner::run_if_asked()` is the first statement of `main` in `lichen` and lichen-tauri. It reads only the arguments, and in runner mode starts nothing of the server. - **Handshake:** protocol 1, refused otherwise. - **Tests:** a test binary names its runner entry (`script_runner_test_entry!`, `set_script_runner`). - **Memory:** the address-space cap is the heap limit plus `RUNNER_BASELINE` (256 MiB). The debug runner's measured peak is 104 MiB. **One parent driver,** `shortcodes/child.rs`, for Python and Lua: - Lua's state runs in the runner, and its answers keep Python's shape. So the error, trace and cache contract is unchanged. - A call past its limit and grace (2 s for Lua, whose own limit answers first) has its child killed, and the next call starts a fresh one. - The abandoned-worker code is now reachable only from JavaScript; O2 deletes it. **Tests this change breaks, fixed here:** - The in-process "abandoned" Lua test becomes `a_call_stuck_in_one_library_call_is_killed_and_the_next_call_runs_at_once`. - The pane test told Pythons apart by PID; it now uses a per-process token. - The namespace-off network test becomes `with_the_network_off_the_filter_refuses_the_sockets_themselves`. - lichen-server's `features` tests register their runner entry. **Plain Docker** (the operator's named check). `e2e/plain-docker/script_shortcodes.sh` (tests PR) passes at the tests tip. - **How it runs:** `docker run --init` with Docker's built-in seccomp profile, no `--cap-add`, no `--security-opt`, as uid 1000, and with `use_sandbox = true`. - **What it builds:** a site with the full-sandbox Python and Lua shortcodes and the `setsid` probe. - **What the published page shows:** - `

HELLO! {"n": 3} 2026-10-08 child

` - `

HELLO! 3 1970

` - `

refused:1

` - **Evidence:** notify-0252420e and notify-c748b3a7. The product code there is this tip's, apart from comments. **Not in O1:** - **O2:** JavaScript. - **O3:** the restored library, and SC-ESC1 and O-C4 for Lua. - **O4:** the timings. - **O5:** mdBook. Checks: `just gate --base 65015486` at a8397539: RAN rust (1389 tests passed, 0 failed), frontends/builtin; SKIPPED lichen-ts, frontends/hugo-cms (unchanged); FAILED none; 0 warnings (notify-6ef099bd). Clippy clean at both tips. Rust: yes. API contract: unchanged.
value.title: Script runtimes O1: Lua runs in lichen's script-runner child; every script child contained by unprivileged means (seccomp, group kill loop, subreaper, Landlock to the proxy port)
